statement: A row of square tiles follows a rule. Picture 1 is a black tile with an arrow pointing up. From each picture to the next, the arrow turns a quarter turn clockwise and the tile switches between black and white. So picture 2 is a white tile with an arrow pointing right. What does picture 23 look like?

choices.text: A black tile with the arrow pointing down
A white tile with the arrow pointing down
choices.misconception: I got the arrow right but thought the odd-numbered pictures are white.

choices.text: A black tile with the arrow pointing left
choices.misconception: I took the remainder 3 from 23 divided by 4 and turned the arrow 3 quarter turns from up, forgetting that picture 1 has had no turns yet.

choices.text: A white tile with the arrow pointing left
choices.misconception: I worked out picture 24 instead of picture 23.

choices.text: A black tile with the arrow pointing up
choices.misconception: I thought the arrow repeats every 2 pictures like the colour does, so every odd picture would match picture 1.

hints: Two things change at once. Track each one on its own.
The arrow repeats every 4 pictures and the colour every 2. Find where picture 23 falls in each cycle separately, then put the two answers together.
Pictures 1, 5, 9, ..., 21 have the arrow pointing up, so picture 22 points right and picture 23 points down. Odd-numbered pictures are black.

solutions.reliable: The arrow goes up, right, down, left and then repeats, so it has a cycle of 4. Picture 21 = 1 + 4 × 5 points up like picture 1, so picture 22 points right and picture 23 points down. The colour has a cycle of 2: odd pictures are black and even pictures are white, so picture 23 is black. Picture 23 is a black tile with the arrow pointing down. The transferable idea: when a pattern changes two things at once, find each cycle separately and then combine them.
solutions.elegant: Picture 23 comes after 22 changes. 22 quarter turns is 5 full turns and 2 more, so the arrow points down; 22 colour switches is an even number, so the tile is black, as at the start.

whyOnTest: Visual patterns often change two features at once; this tests describing each change separately before choosing the next picture.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
